_notes: Static, manually-built, deterministic asset. NOT generated by any model.
data/zho/catalog.json stores only transliterated English letter names (e.g. 'Alif', 'Meem') with no Arabic glyph field, so this mapping cannot be derived automatically from the catalog alone.

Built by matching each entry's Sitecore item-suffix ID (e.g. Alif_4846, Baa_4847, ...) against the ZHO site's own display ordering, which runs in exact standard Arabic abjad order (ا ب ت ث ج ح خ د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ع غ ف ق ك ل م ن ه و ي) followed by taa marbuta, the four hamza-position variants, and the two definite-article entries (Al, Laa) - 28 base letters + 7 extras = 35, matching data/zho/coverage_report.md's documented Alphabets count.

Resolves the two ambiguities coverage_report.md explicitly flagged: 'Taa' (id 17fd4d03...) = regular taa (ت), 'Taa' (id 4c82e730...) = taa marbuta (ة, Arabic-locale title 'تاء مربوطة'); 'Haa' (id 4c670667...) = ه (regular haa, position 26 in abjad order), 'Haa' (id c1a43a99...) = ح (pharyngeal haa, position 6). NOT ط, which is its own separate entry labeled 'Tua'.

fingerspell.py should decompose an Arabic word into base letters only (no diacritics) and look up each letter's 'catalog_id' below. Letters not present as a plain base-alphabet entry here (e.g. word contains a taa marbuta ة mid-word vs word-final, or an alif variant like أ/إ/آ) must be normalized to their base form before lookup; any letter that still fails lookup makes the containing unit UNSUPPORTED, not silently skipped.

letters.note: definite article ligature, not a base letter - used only if a term's translated Arabic form includes the definite article and the resolver chooses to sign it explicitly
lam-alif ligature, not decomposed into separate laam+alif when it occurs, since ZHO signs it as one unit
